sourceOccurrences.label: Degree and boundary first moments
sourceOccurrences.note: PMHN distinguishes raw incident coordinates from loop-free graph degree. SZLN gives adjacency marginals, measurable countable degree, the extended expectation and Markov bound; the source also includes the tautological zero-threshold case. TOTD covers finite pair sets on arbitrary vertices and outgoing boundary pairs on countable vertices. A crossing bond is counted once, through its orientation out of the finite set. The first-moment identities use only marginals; no infinite-expectation implication is inferred without independence.

sourceOccurrences.label: Incident-coordinate products and isolation
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete grouped source contracts with additional infinite-product deductions
sourceOccurrences.note: TEYJ includes extended nonnegative generating parameters, the one-coordinate factor, mutual independence and the finite zero-parameter product. TYZP interprets the pointwise infimum of powers as the generating function of the limiting count only for parameters in [0,1], with 0^0 = 1 and 1^infinity = 1. UNJ6 erases the root from each exhaustion set. The source exports the isolation product but not the additional positivity characterization or XJ74 infinite-row deduction.

sourceOccurrences.label: Finite counts from indicator sums
sourceOccurrences.note: The arbitrary-set extended cardinality identity and finite indicator expectation are explained before CPD6. TOTD retains its existing bond-specific statement. No uncountable Tonelli interchange is claimed.

sourceOccurrences.label: Finite independent-count laws and concentration
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete grouped source contracts with elementary expository extensions
sourceOccurrences.note: CPD6 supplies the binomial specialization and the more general assignment sum. XSA6 proves the centered exponential-moment bound and both one-sided tails, with the empty coordinate set stated separately rather than using division by zero. The two-sided bound is an expository union-bound consequence. Raw pair counts may include loops; graph degree excludes them. No random-coordinate-set concentration or cluster-volume concentration follows.

sourceOccurrences.label: Infinite rows and zero critical intensity
sourceOccurrences.note: XJ74 gives the infinite-degree conclusion by the product generating function. The source instead uses the second Borel–Cantelli lemma. VNRG supplies the finite-intensity truncation estimate and the root/global threshold consequences at one specified vertex. No transitivity, uniform row hypothesis or claim about other roots is added.

proofUses.reason: The degree is the countable sum of off-diagonal adjacency indicators.
Incident pair coordinates are distinct, so their measurable factors are independent and their nonnegative expectation factors.
Increasing counts give decreasing bounded powers when the generating parameter lies in [0,1].
The zero-parameter limit gives isolation; elementary logarithmic bounds characterize positivity of the infinite product.
The finite first moment gives finite degree. If the row diverges, the generating function vanishes at every fixed parameter strictly between zero and one.
Finite assignment probabilities factor over independent coordinates; summing the assignments gives the count law.
Independence factors centered exponential moments. The single-coordinate bound follows by differentiating its log moment generating function.
Truncate the divergent finite intensity row, compare it to the probability row, then apply the independent degree criterion and the threshold definitions.
A definition; it invokes no other wiki assertion.
